applicant_utility.summary: KTH asks for almost no paperwork, which means the scholarship is effectively decided by what is already in your universityadmissions.se file - so the real deadline is the 2 February document deadline, not the 15 January scholarship deadline. Everything hinges on ranking KTH first: a second, third or fourth priority programme cannot be awarded the scholarship at all, no matter how strong the record. Because the award is tuition-only and explicitly excludes living costs, treat it as a fee waiver and arrange the Migration Agency-compliant living-cost funding separately. The published nomination rate - 65 out of 718 admitted applicants in 2026, or about 9% - tells you this is a reach award, so pair it with a solid financial fallback. Note that the second-year continuation is conditional on satisfactory first-year results, so the waiver is not guaranteed across the full programme.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fee-paying applicants to an eligible two-year KTH master's with a strong GPA, a well-regarded awarding university, and demonstrable research, work or sustainability achievements.
application_readiness_checklist: Rank the KTH programme first at universityadmissions.se and pay the application fee before the national deadline
Upload every supporting document to universityadmissions.se well before 2 February, since KTH reuses them rather than asking for new ones
Prepare a short written account of how a KTH master's degree lets you contribute to the sustainable development goals, as the form asks for it
Check your programme against the eligible and excluded lists - Erasmus+, EIT and Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering applicants belong in a different scholarship
Submit the KTH scholarship form in the 1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 window and diarise the 1 April 2027 result date
common_rejection_risks: KTH ranked second, third or fourth at universityadmissions.se, which makes the application ineligible outright
Missing the 2 February document deadline, which starves the scholarship evaluation of the evidence it relies on
Applying to a joint Erasmus+, EIT or Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering programme
Not meeting the admission requirements of the programme applied for, since only admitted applicants are nominated
Submitting a generic sustainability statement instead of a specific, personal one tied to the chosen programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Stockholm, travel, insurance and the application fee; the second-year tuition if first-year results are not satisfactory.
document_audit: There is no scholarship upload - the form reuses your universityadmissions.se documents, so those documents are your scholarship documents
Your application must show KTH as first priority; second-choice applications are never assessed for the scholarship
The 2 February document deadline is a national deadline, not a KTH one, so late courier delivery is a real risk
Applicants to joint programmes excluded from this scholarship should use the KTH Joint Programme Scholarship instead
The one-year Architectural Lighting Design programme is eligible, so do not assume it is excluded by length
alerts: The second year of the waiver is conditional on satisfactory first-year study results
The scholarship form is only live between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027 - it is not a standing application
Results land on 1 April 2027, late in the permit and housing planning cycle, so do not defer travel bookings to that date
Applicants to joint Erasmus+, EIT and Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering programmes must apply to the KTH Joint Programme Scholarship instead
Separate KTH One-Year and KTH India Scholarships exist, but for different applicant profiles
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: universityadmissions.se application with KTH as first priority plus documents by 2 February, then the short KTH online form during December-January, with results on 1 April 2027.
